title: Five European countries plan a rejected-asylum-seeker return hub in Rwanda; no agreement has been signed
summary: Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands are planning a “return hub” in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers and are consulting the U.N. refugee agency about human-rights compliance. AP reported that no agreement had been signed.
context: The proposal places Rwanda again at the centre of Europe’s externalized migration policy and could create a new state-revenue and diplomatic channel. It also revives legal and rights questions raised by earlier transfer arrangements. The plan remains a proposal. Its legal terms, financing, oversight and implementation timeline are unresolved.

title: Sudanese army airstrike kills at least 13 people in West Kordofan, rights group says
summary: The Emergency Lawyers group said a Sudanese army airstrike on Abu Qalb village near Abu Zabad in West Kordofan killed at least 13 people, with women and children among the dead. AP said it could not independently verify the reported toll.
context: The report adds another civilian-harm record as fighting shifts across Kordofan and supply routes remain contested. It underscores the difficulty of independently verifying casualties and responsibility in active war zones. The casualty count and attribution come from Emergency Lawyers and were not independently verified by AP.

title: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass forces along their border as war fears rise
summary: Conflict monitors and people tied to rival militias told Reuters that Ethiopia and Eritrea had amassed forces along their shared border. ACLED reported artillery shelling and armed clashes near Badme, while another militia-linked source disputed that the two national armies had clashed.
context: The buildup raises the risk that renewed fighting in Tigray expands into a direct interstate conflict, threatening trade routes, displacement patterns and regional diplomacy across the Horn. Reuters could not independently confirm reported skirmishes. Ethiopia did not respond to Reuters, and Eritrea rejected what it called propaganda without directly addressing the buildup.
